name: adaptive-nowcasting (tourism)
what_it_holds: R repository implementing 'Adaptive Nowcasting of Tourism Statistics using Google Trends' — a method paper/code specifically for tourism-statistics nowcasting from Trends data (not consumption or GDP generically).
why_useful: Directly on-theme: a tourism-specific (not generic macro) Google-Trends nowcasting method, addressing gap #17 (mixed-frequency/nowcasting methods) with a travel-demand application closer to Airbnb nights than the generic GDP/consumption nowcasting repos below. Worth reading the method even though our own generic Trends nowcast failed — this uses an adaptive/rolling weighting scheme we have not tried.
geography: unspecified (method paper, likely a national tourism board case study)
duplicate_of_holding: overlaps failed 'Google Trends as pulled' test but is a different (adaptive) method, not yet tried
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: Directly on-theme: a tourism-specific (not generic macro) Google-Trends nowcasting method, addressing gap #17 (mixed-frequency/nowcasting methods) with a travel-demand application closer to Airbnb nights than the generic GDP/consumption nowcasting repos below. Worth reading the method even though our own generic Trends nowcast failed — this uses an adaptive/rolling weighting scheme we have not tried.

name: Tourism-data-analysis
what_it_holds: Single committed file `travel_data.xls` used to analyze top tourist-sending and top tourist-receiving countries and trend of the international travel & tourism sector. Exact source, years, and country list not confirmed from the fetched page (needs opening the xls to verify).
why_useful: One of the few repos directly citing a WTTC report as its data source; worth checking for a committed WTTC economic-impact extract (GDP/employment contribution by country), which would plug directly into the WTTC gap in this theme, though the repo is stale (2019) so any data would be pre-2019 vintage only.
themes: Tourism satellite accounts and tourism spending data: WTTC, UNWTO, BEA travel and tourism satellite account, national tourism expenditure surveys

name: china-tourism-dataset
what_it_holds: Single committed CSV `china_tourism_2015_2023.csv` (12.6KB), 31 Chinese provinces/regions x 9 years (2015-2023): columns year, province, domestic_tourists_mln, inbound_tourists_mln, tourism_revenue_billion, gdp_billion, population_mln. E.g. Beijing 2015: domestic 199.75mn, inbound 9.168mn, tourism revenue RMB190.63bn. Appears compiled from official (NBS/provincial statistical yearbook) tourism figures; no source citation or code, just the flat file. No commit history/stars visible beyond the single file; unclear licence.
why_useful: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, China domestic+inbound) with province-level granularity and a longer 9-year run; could be cross-checked/extended for a China domestic-travel base rate, though ABNB's China exposure is minor so relevance is mostly as a macro-context comparator, not a KPI driver.
themes: China outbound and domestic travel data: CNTA/Ministry stats, Ctrip reports, Chinese holiday travel datasets, Hong Kong/Macau arrivals
why_all: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, China domestic+inbound) with province-level granularity and a longer 9-year run; could be cross-checked/extended for a China domestic-travel base rate, though ABNB's China exposure is minor so relevance is mostly as a macro-context comparator, not a KPI driver.

name: _baiduqianxi_ (Baidu Migration Platform API client)
what_it_holds: Python client (87 stars, updated ~13 days ago per search snapshot) for Baidu Qianxi ("Baidu Migration"/慧眼) — China's near-real-time population-flow index built from Baidu Maps location data, giving city-to-city and intra-city movement intensity indices, historically used by researchers/media to track Chunyun (Spring Festival travel rush) and holiday travel surges since ~2015.
why_useful: Baidu Qianxi is the closest thing to a real-time China domestic-travel-intensity proxy (used academically for COVID mobility and holiday-travel studies); a pull method for it would let the team build a China domestic travel-intensity index analogous to TSA throughput, addressing gap #7/#20-style mobility proxies, though it requires validating against any China revenue-relevant KPI (currently unclear if worth building given ABNB's small China footprint).
themes: China outbound and domestic travel data: CNTA/Ministry stats, Ctrip reports, Chinese holiday travel datasets, Hong Kong/Macau arrivals
why_all: Baidu Qianxi is the closest thing to a real-time China domestic-travel-intensity proxy (used academically for COVID mobility and holiday-travel studies); a pull method for it would let the team build a China domestic travel-intensity index analogous to TSA throughput, addressing gap #7/#20-style mobility proxies, though it requires validating against any China revenue-relevant KPI (currently unclear if worth building given ABNB's small China footprint).

name: China_Outbound_Tourism
what_it_holds: data/ folder with 9 committed CSVs: Age.csv, Consumption.csv, Income.csv, Marriage.csv, Outbound_travelers_by_province.csv, Spending.csv, TopPlace.csv, TourismExpenditure1995_2013.csv, population.csv, plus a china.json map. A student data-viz project profiling Chinese outbound tourist demographics and spending; TourismExpenditure1995_2013.csv gives a long (18-year) historical outbound-expenditure series and Outbound_travelers_by_province.csv gives province-level outbound traveler counts. No license stated; last activity ~2017 (repo old, data itself covers 1995-2013).
why_useful: Fills gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) and gap #9 context (Chinese outbound demand, relevant to APAC mix and Chinese-traveler share of ABNB bookings) with genuinely historical (pre-2013) province-level and time-series data not covered by anything we hold.
time_coverage: ~1995-2013 (TourismExpenditure series); other files single-snapshot demographic breakdowns, era unclear
size_hint: 9 small CSVs, unknown row counts (not row-counted, file listing only)
